rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to elute all 6 compounds if possible and map the overall elution window without excessive truncation risk. This should reveal whether peaks are compressed early, late, or across the full gradient so later runs can tighten the window and adjust slope.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only gain is faster elution. The peaks span roughly phi_e about 0.15 to 0.54, so a narrower, shorter gradient ending at 0.75 should keep all compounds in-gradient while cutting t_last substantially.

Resolution has a large safety margin, so push for the last 0.31 min by making the gradient slightly steeper and raising temperature one step. This should bring the last peak under 10 min while still leaving ample separation.

We already have the maximum CRF, so now map how far we can compress before any pair approaches 1.5. This more aggressive method should still keep all peaks in the gradient and tests the margin for a faster operating point.

The worst pair still has substantial margin, so compress further to find the practical edge of full resolution. This tests whether a still steeper, hotter method can remain at CRF 1.000 while reducing run time further.

The limiting pair is 1/2, and the loss at injection 5 likely came from the extra temperature step as much as the steepness. Keep the very fast 4 min, 0.65 endpoint method but back off to 50 C to see if that pair recovers above 1.5 while preserving a short run.

At 4 min and 50 C we have full resolution with margin, so narrow the window slightly to put more of the gradient into the observed elution range and test whether the critical 1/2 pair stays above 1.5. This may further optimize the fast method while keeping all compounds in-gradient or near the hold transition.

The 4 min methods still have resolution margin, so test the shortest allowed gradient at the successful 0.65 endpoint and 50 C. This probes whether the critical 1/2 pair remains resolved under maximal compression while likely giving the fastest fully resolved run yet.

The 2 min run failed only on the first pair, so use the shortest gradient but a slightly narrower window to make the early segment shallower, which should preferentially help pair 1/2. This tests whether 2 min is recoverable without giving up the very short run time.

At 4 min and 50 C the critical pair is only just above threshold, so lowering temperature one step should improve that margin while keeping the same fast gradient. This checks whether 45 C gives a more robust fully resolved operating point with only a small time penalty.

The 2 min runs failed only on the first pair, and lowering temperature improved that pair substantially at 4 min. Test whether the shortest gradient becomes fully resolved at 45 C, which would define an even faster optimal method.

The last peak at 4 min, 0.60 endpoint still comes out at 7.4 min and the limiting pair actually improved, suggesting we can narrow the window further from the high-organic side. This tests whether a 0.55 endpoint keeps all six peaks eluting with full resolution while concentrating the gradient even more tightly on the useful phi range.

The first pair is the only real constraint, and its strong temperature sensitivity suggests selectivity changes matter. Probe a hotter but shallower method to see whether 55 C can still maintain full resolution when slope is relaxed, which helps map the temperature/selectivity tradeoff around the critical pair.

At 55 C the 4 min, 0.65 endpoint was just too aggressive for pair 1/2, so slightly widening the gradient window may shift their elution to a less compressed region and restore resolution. This tests whether a hotter fast method can still be fully resolved with a modest endpoint increase.

The best fast fully resolved point found is 4 min, 0.65, 50 C, and 2 min is too steep; a 6 min run at the same window and temperature will show how much extra resolution margin the critical 1/2 pair gains from slope alone. This helps define the robustness curve around the current optimum without changing the selectivity conditions.

Since 4 min at 0.65 works at both 45 and 50 C, test a slightly wider window at the cooler setting to map robustness of the critical first pair under a different slope/temperature balance. This helps confirm whether the current 4 min, 0.65, 50 C point is truly the fastest practical fully resolved condition.

The 4 min, 0.70, 45 C method is fully resolved with comfortable margin and already faster than the 0.65 endpoint at 45 C, so push the endpoint one more step higher. This checks whether the last peak can be pulled even earlier while keeping the critical 1/2 pair above 1.5.

The 4 min, 0.75, 45 C run is fully resolved and faster still, with the critical pair retaining some margin. Increase the endpoint one more step to see if the last peak can be shortened further before pair 1/2 falls below the 1.5 threshold.

The trend from phi1 0.70 to 0.80 at 4 min and 45 C is monotonic: faster runs while the critical 1/2 pair remains above 1.5, though margin is shrinking. One more endpoint increase should locate the edge of full resolution and may yield the fastest successful method so far.

At 4 min and 45 C, raising phi1 from 0.70 to 0.85 has steadily shortened t_last while pair 1/2 approaches the resolution limit, so the next endpoint step should locate the boundary. This may deliver the fastest fully resolved method if the first pair remains just above 1.5.

Since 0.90 at 45 C just crossed below the threshold on pair 1/2, keep the near-best 0.85 endpoint but lower temperature one step to increase resolution margin while preserving the very short 4 min gradient. This tests whether the same fast window remains fully resolved under a slightly cooler, more robust selectivity setting.

At 45 C, phi1 0.90 was only slightly below the resolution threshold, and lowering temperature to 40 C at phi1 0.85 restored substantial margin for pair 1/2. Test 0.90 at 40 C to see if it becomes the fastest fully resolved method.

The trend at 4 min and 40 C shows increasing phi1 keeps shortening the run while the critical pair still has comfortable margin at 0.90. Test the maximum endpoint to see whether it remains fully resolved and gives the fastest successful method available on the grid.

The first pair remains the limiting one even at the fastest fully resolved method, and both earliest peaks are still retained rather than unretained. Raising phi0 one step while keeping the successful fast high-endpoint method tests whether the entire run can be compressed a bit more without pushing pair 1/2 below 1.5.

Injection 24 improved both speed and the critical 1/2 resolution, so there is room to raise the starting organic one more step. This final run tests whether further front-end compression gives the fastest fully resolved method on the grid while keeping the first pair above 1.5.
